title: Tell the AI who you're writing for

entries.text: Tell markoto who you're writing for

Every doc carries four context fields beyond the title: a description, a target audience, a language, and the template it was created from. The AI sees them on every prompt, so a one-time minute setting them up saves you re-typing context on every "rewrite this" / "extend this" / "draft a section".

entries.caption: Tap the Info tab on the bottom bar
The Document panel opens, Description, Language, Audience, Template, all editable in place.

entries.text: Set the audience, language, and description

Description is one line that tells the AI what this document IS. Audience is a closed enum of writing registers (six of them, each with a tuned tone fragment). Language is free text, six curated presets plus typed input for anything else.

entries.caption: The description is captured, the AI will see this on every prompt.

entries.text: Ask the AI for an intro

With audience + language + description set, ANY prompt the AI sees gets shaped by them, without you mentioning audience or language in your prompt. We ask for a one-line intro in plain English; the AI returns marketing-tone Deutsch.

entries.caption: Click into the AI prompt bar
The prompt bar lifts and glows, ready for your prompt.
The ask is short and English. The audience + language fields do the rest of the work.
The AI is working, the bar pulses until it is done.
The AI added a one-line intro in German with a marketing tone, although the draft and the prompt are English: the document settings did that.
